findings.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:22 — start/end/statsPeriod params were removed from the serializer and the datetime__range filter dropped, so callers sending a date range now silently receive the org's entire unfiltered audit history (DRF ignores unknown params, no 400) and the previous validation errors for malformed ranges are gone.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on a datetime (order_by="-datetime"), which raises TypeError; build_cursor invokes key(results[0]) and key(results[-1]) for any non-empty page, so every optimized request with at least one row returns a 500.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:843 — value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value which build_queryset injects as `datetime <= <int>` in raw SQL extra(where=...), producing a Postgres operator-mismatch DB error (500) for any cursor with a nonzero value; DateTimePaginator's timestamp conversion was dropped.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — enable_advanced is evaluated unconditionally (even when optimized_pagination is absent) and dereferences organization_context.member.has_global_access; for principals without an OrganizationMember (e.g. sentry-app/integration tokens with org:write) member is None and the whole endpoint 500s, a regression for all callers.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — The "administrator" gate is has_global_access, which is true for owners/managers and for every member of an open-membership (allow_joinleave) org, and request.user.is_superuser is checked without is_active_superuser(request); the gate does not restrict to admins as the comments claim.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — Shared BasePaginator change affects all cursor-paginated endpoints: a negative offset with is_prev=1 is passed straight through to QuerySet slicing (ValueError -> 500), while a negative offset with is_prev=0 is silently clamped to 0 but build_cursor still uses the raw negative cursor.offset (next_offset = offset + limit) so the next cursor drifts backward and pages overlap/repeat rows; inconsistent and the comment about "queryset handles boundary conditions" is wrong.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — PR is titled as a performance change but neither code path changes query shape, indexes, or cost; the only behavioral changes are removed date filtering and a new (broken) negative-offset cursor mode, so the "performance" framing does not match the mechanics.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:22 — No tests were added or updated despite removing public query params and adding a new paginator/feature flag; existing audit-log tests exercising statsPeriod/start/end filtering would now fail or be silently untested.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — New optimized_pagination query param is not declared in AuditLogQueryParamSerializer, not documented anywhere, and selects a different cursor encoding, so cursors are not portable between the two modes of the same endpoint.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — organization_context.member.has_global_access is evaluated on every request (not just optimized ones), and member is None for non-member callers such as sentry-app/integration tokens, so those existing clients now get an AttributeError 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — Clamping a negative non-prev offset to 0 silently serves page 0 but build_cursor still uses the negative cursor.offset (next_offset = offset + limit, has_prev truthy), producing an overlapping/skewed next cursor where previously the request failed loudly

adjudication.rationale: In `BasePaginator.get_result` the diff changes slicing to clamp `start_offset = max(0, offset)` for non-`prev` cursors, but it leaves `offset = cursor.offset` unchanged. Subsequent logic still uses `offset` (e.g., `len(results) == offset + limit + extra`) and passes the original `cursor` into `build_cursor(...)`, so any negative `cursor.offset` will be treated as page 0 for the query but still generate cursors/has_prev based on a negative offset. Previously, `queryset[offset:stop]` with a negative offset would have raised (Django queryset negative slicing), so this change can silently alter behavior and produce inconsistent/overlapping cursors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:845 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a near-verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result (only the offset-slice lines differ); should be an override hook on the base rather than duplicating ~60 lines that will drift.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `OptimizedCursorPaginator(BasePaginator)` adds a full `get_result(...)` implementation (~80 lines) that mirrors the existing paginator `get_result` flow (cursor defaulting, limit clamp, hits counting, queryset build, offset/extra logic, prev handling/reverse, `build_cursor`, post_query_filter). The primary intentional difference is the slicing/start_offset handling for negative offsets when `enable_advanced_features` is on. This is a concrete maintainability/architecture issue (duplication likely to drift) rather than an immediate correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877 — The two branches at 877-885 produce identical slices in every case that Django accepts (negative start raises AssertionError "Negative indexing is not supported"), so the "advanced" branch and the enable_advanced_features flag are dead/misleading and the comment "Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, the “advanced” path explicitly allows `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`, and then slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices and raises an AssertionError, so this branch will fail at runtime if a negative offset cursor is supplied. Because negative slicing isn’t actually supported, the `enable_advanced_features` branch is effectively dead/misleading and the comment claiming Django “properly handles negative slicing automatically” is false; additionally, the non-advanced path already behaves the same for non-negative offsets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 — get_item_key/value_from_cursor are exact copies of Paginator's int-based versions, yet the class replaces DateTimePaginator on a "-datetime" order_by, so math.floor(datetime) will TypeError; the type boundary between int cursors and datetime cursors leaks and the class should subclass DateTimePaginator (or Paginator) instead of copy-pasting.

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the new path swaps `DateTimePaginator` for `OptimizedCursorPaginator` while still paginating with `order_by="-datetime"`. `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key()` does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` and then `math.floor(value)`/`math.ceil(value)`, which will raise `TypeError` if `value` is a `datetime` (as audit log `datetime` fields typically are). Unlike `DateTimePaginator`, this class does not convert datetimes to numeric cursor keys, so using it on a datetime-ordered queryset is broken behavior introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:84 — enable_advanced_features=True is threaded through Endpoint.paginate(**paginator_kwargs) as an untyped pass-through kwarg and is always True whenever OptimizedCursorPaginator is selected, so the flag is redundant with the class choice and couples the endpoint to a paginator-private option.

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, when `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is chosen, the endpoint always passes `enable_advanced_features=True` (constant) into `self.paginate(...)`. The new paginator’s `__init__` in `api/paginator.py` already exposes `enable_advanced_features` (default `False`), so the endpoint is now explicitly depending on a paginator-specific toggle, and the flag is redundant in this endpoint because it is never set to `False` when that paginator class is selected. The claim about `Endpoint.paginate` being an “untyped pass-through” can’t be verified from this diff alone, but the redundancy/coupling is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — optimized_pagination is read raw from request.GET instead of going through AuditLogQueryParamSerializer like every other query param, splitting input validation across two places.

adjudication.rationale: In organization_auditlogs.py the new flag is read directly from the raw query string (`use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"`) rather than being part of the existing validated `query` data used for other params (e.g., `query["event"]`). This splits parameter handling/validation across two mechanisms and makes behavior dependent on exact string matching (only "true" works), which is a real review issue but not a clear correctness/security defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179 — BasePaginator now introduces start_offset that only differs from offset for negative non-prev cursors (which it clamps) while still passing negative offsets through on is_prev (which Django rejects), and line 188 still compares against the un-clamped offset; the new comment claiming the queryset "will handle boundary conditions" is inaccurate.

adjudication.rationale: In BasePaginator.get_result the diff introduces `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` and slices with `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, but later logic still uses the original `offset` (e.g. `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra:`). If `offset` is negative and clamped to 0, this condition becomes incorrect. Additionally, for `cursor.is_prev` the code still allows `start_offset = offset` (potentially negative) and then slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, which can break since Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative start indices. The comment claiming the queryset will handle boundary conditions is therefore inaccurate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:822 — Docstring claims "optimized query path", "streamlined boundary handling" and "performance optimizations" but the class performs no optimization and issues the same query as BasePaginator; misleading documentation.

adjudication.rationale: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` docstring advertises an “optimized query path” and “performance optimizations,” but in the diff the implementation largely duplicates the existing offset-slicing approach (`results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`) and does not show any concrete query/ORM optimization beyond an optional negative-offset slicing branch when `enable_advanced_features` is set. So the documentation appears to overclaim relative to what’s verifiably implemented in this diff (even if there is a small behavioral difference).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26 — Comment-only no-op change asserting a "performance optimization" that does not exist; no code changed in this file.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/utils/cursors.py` the only change is adding comments above `self.offset = int(offset)`; there is no behavioral/code change in that file. The new comment claims a "performance optimization" / "allow negative offsets" but the code already accepted negative ints before and nothing was implemented here, so the comment is misleading/no-op as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:23 — Stray blank line added after the serializer class line; trailing whitespace at lines 72 and 89 and at paginator.py:824,827,829; three blank lines at paginator.py:818-820 will be rewritten by black/flake8.

adjudication.rationale: The cited issues are purely formatting/style nits (extra blank lines and trailing whitespace). The diff does show multiple blank lines before `class OptimizedCursorPaginator` in `paginator.py` and at least one trailing space (e.g., `order_by="-datetime", ` in `organization_auditlogs.py`), but these are not defects or substantive review issues under the provided categories. The claim about a "stray blank line" at `organization_auditlogs.py:23`/specific line numbers can’t be verified from the shown hunks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:24 — Removing start/end/statsPeriod drops the only way to bound the (organization_id, datetime) index range scan, so event/actor-filtered queries on high-volume orgs must walk the org's entire history to fill a page instead of a narrow window.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not remove any start/end/statsPeriod parameters or related filtering logic in `organization_auditlogs.py`. The only visible changes are adding an optional `OptimizedCursorPaginator` path gated by `optimized_pagination=true` and admin access, plus paginator logic changes to offset handling. Since no time-bounding filters are deleted or modified in this diff, the finding’s claim about dropping the only way to bound an `(organization_id, datetime)` index scan is not supported by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:845 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result that issues the identical SQL (same WHERE/ORDER BY/LIMIT), so it delivers zero performance improvement over DateTimePaginator while adding a second code path to maintain.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` is not a verbatim copy of the existing paginator logic: it adds an `enable_advanced_features` flag, introduces a distinct branch that allows `start_offset = cursor.offset` when negative (`if self.enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0:`), and has different offset handling comments/flow. Also, the claim about issuing “identical SQL” / “zero performance improvement over DateTimePaginator” cannot be verified from the diff alone (SQL depends on `build_queryset`, ordering, and Django slicing behavior), and `DateTimePaginator` vs `OptimizedCursorPaginator` are different classes with different semantics in this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:842 — value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value which build_queryset injects as `datetime <= %s` against a timestamptz column, producing a DB error (or an unindexed cast) instead of the indexed datetime range predicate DateTimePaginator produces.

adjudication.rationale: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is wired into `organization_auditlogs.py` with `order_by="-datetime"`, implying pagination is keyed off a datetime field. But `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key()` does `math.floor/ceil` on `getattr(item, self.key)` and returns an `int`, and `value_from_cursor()` returns the cursor value unchanged. If `self.key` is `datetime`, `math.floor(datetime)` will raise (or, if the cursor value is an int, it won’t match the datetime field semantics used by the queryset filtering in `build_queryset`). Either way, this paginator is not compatible with datetime-key pagination as used here, causing broken pagination/possible DB type issues when the optimized path is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 — get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on a datetime and raises TypeError on any non-empty page, so the optimized path executes the DB query and then fails before returning, wasting the query on every request.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key`, it does `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` on `value = getattr(item, self.key)`. In `organization_auditlogs.get`, the paginator is used with `order_by="-datetime"`, so the key will be the model’s `datetime` field (a `datetime` object). `math.floor/ceil` on a `datetime` raises `TypeError`, so the optimized pagination path will fetch results and then fail when building cursors for any non-empty page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 — The "negative offset" fast path slices queryset[negative:...], which Django rejects with AssertionError("Negative indexing is not supported"), so the advertised bidirectional optimization is dead code that only produces 500s.

adjudication.rationale: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` adds an “advanced” path that intentionally slices with a negative start (`start_offset = cursor.offset` when `cursor.offset < 0`), i.e. `queryset[start_offset:stop]` (paginator.py ~880+). The surrounding comments claim Django ORM “properly handles negative slicing automatically”, but Django `QuerySet` slicing does not support negative indices and will raise at runtime, turning this advertised optimization into a 500-producing path when hit. The earlier change in `BasePaginator.get_result` also still allows negative `offset` when `cursor.is_prev` (uses `start_offset = ... else offset`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — BasePaginator now silently clamps negative offsets to 0 for non-prev cursors, changing shared behaviour for every paginator in the codebase with no performance benefit.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` around the shown `get_result`, the diff replaces `queryset[offset:stop]` with `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` and then slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. This does indeed silently clamp negative `offset` values to 0 for non-`prev` cursors, changing behavior in the shared paginator path. Whether there is “no performance benefit” can’t be proven from the diff, but the behavior/scope change itself is real and worth review even if it doesn’t necessarily constitute a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated unconditionally (before `use_optimized` is checked) and `member` is None for non-member principals (Sentry App / org auth tokens with org:write, superusers-without-membership are only saved by short-circuit), so those callers now get an AttributeError/500 on every audit-log request regardless of the new query param.
matched_golden_ids: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same root bug: `organization_context.member` can be `None` for API key/org auth token/non-member principals, and line 71 unconditionally accesses `organization_context.member.has_global_access` without a None-check, leading to an AttributeError/500 despite valid org scopes. The candidate additionally claims it happens regardless of the query param due to unconditional evaluation, but the underlying issue matches the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — has_global_access` is not an admin check: it is True for every member of an open-membership org (allow_joinleave) and any member with a global role, so the "authorized administrators" gate described in the comments is effectively bypassable by ordinary members; the comment misrepresents the privilege boundary.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` gating the optimized paginator, but it does not define what `has_global_access` means or when it is true. The finding’s claim that `has_global_access` is true for ordinary members of open-membership orgs (and thus bypasses an “admin” gate) relies on external semantics not present in the diff, so it cannot be verified from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:821 — New OptimizedCursorPaginator (with a datetime key, get_item_key calls math.floor on a datetime and will TypeError on any non-empty page) ships with zero unit tests, so this crash is uncaught.

adjudication.rationale: The new OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` and then calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on that value before casting to int. In organization_auditlogs.py, the new code uses `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, so the paginator key is plausibly `datetime` (a datetime object on AuditLogEntry). `math.floor(datetime_obj)` would raise a TypeError on any non-empty result set, causing a runtime crash when the optimized path is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — Shared BasePaginator.get_result slicing changed for all endpoints (is_prev now passes raw offset, and a negative cursor offset makes Django raise "Negative indexing is not supported") with no paginator test added or updated to cover prev/negative-offset paths.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change shared pagination slicing logic in `BasePaginator.get_result` (now clamping `offset` to 0 only for non-prev: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, then slicing `queryset[start_offset:stop]`). It also introduces `OptimizedCursorPaginator` that explicitly allows negative `cursor.offset` and slices with a negative `start_offset` when `enable_advanced_features` is true. No tests are added/updated in this diff to cover the new/changed offset/prev-path behavior. However, the finding’s claim that `is_prev` “now” passes raw offset is not clearly a regression (prev already used `offset` directly before), and whether Django will raise on negative slicing is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:22 — start/end/statsPeriod filtering was removed but no endpoint tests were touched; unknown query params are silently ignored by the serializer, so any existing date-filter tests would either fail or silently return unfiltered rows, and no test asserts the new behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The shown diff for `organization_auditlogs.py` only changes pagination behavior (imports `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, adds `optimized_pagination`/admin gating, and switches paginator classes). There is no diff evidence that `start`/`end`/`statsPeriod` filtering was removed, nor any serializer/query-param handling changes related to date filters. Test changes are also not shown, but the core claim (date filtering removed and silently ignored) is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — The optimized_pagination admin gate (superuser / has_global_access, and the organization_context.member-is-None case for non-member superusers) has no positive or negative authorization test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new nontrivial authorization gating logic for the new `optimized_pagination` path (`use_optimized = request.GET.get(...)` and `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`). No tests are shown being added/updated in this diff to cover either the allowed/denied behavior of this gate, and the new expression also introduces an edge-case surface (`organization_context.member` could be `None`, making `.has_global_access` unsafe if the superuser short-circuit doesn’t apply). This is a specific, diff-grounded testing gap rather than a proven runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877 — enable_advanced_features negative-offset branch has no test; its comment claims the ORM "properly handles negative slicing" which is false, so the untested path 500s.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` the new `enable_advanced_features` branch explicitly allows `start_offset = cursor.offset` when it is negative and then slices the Django `queryset[start_offset:stop]` (around line ~877 in the diff). Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices, so this can raise at runtime (500) if a negative offset cursor is supplied. The comment asserting the ORM “properly handles negative slicing” is therefore misleading, and the diff introduces a reachable crash path for `optimized_pagination=true` with `enable_advanced_features=True`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:28 — Cursor now documents accepting negative offsets but no cursor parsing/round-trip test exercises a negative offset, and the review environment is a 3-file snapshot with no tests directory or pytest, so existing suites could not be run to confirm impact.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces and documents “negative offset” behavior (comment added in `src/sentry/utils/cursors.py` and logic in `src/sentry/api/paginator.py`, plus the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` branch that explicitly allows `cursor.offset < 0` and slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]`). No corresponding tests or validation/round-trip coverage are shown in the diff to exercise this new negative-offset cursor behavior, which is a specific gap given the new nontrivial pagination path.
